memory_update.text: PWR should remain the reference leader for grid-construction and large-load-center infrastructure exposure, but it is too well-covered to be the primary underfollowed alpha candidate.
POWL is a high-priority discovery-lane candidate because its switchgear and power-control exposure is directly tied to data-center power equipment and behind-the-meter generation designs.
MYRG is a lower-attention electrical-construction candidate to track for substation, T&D, and data-center C&I execution leverage.
LEU belongs in the speculative-shadow lane for nuclear-fuel and HALEU linkage to firm-power procurement, but it needs explicit contract evidence before promotion to a stronger node relation.

Next searches should expand beyond direct leaders into transformer specialists, substation component suppliers, testing/inspection providers, permitting/grid-study software, and regional utilities with unusually large data-center load-growth exposure.

node: Grid interconnection, transmission construction, utility power availability, nuclear/firm power, and data-center energy procurement
summary: Layer 1B expands the direct public-company universe for the AI/data-center power-availability node. The reference lane is anchored by Quanta Services as the obvious grid-construction leader. The discovery lane emphasizes narrower or less universally owned public companies with direct exposure to medium-voltage switchgear, electrical construction, and nuclear-fuel availability: Powell Industries, MYR Group, and Centrus Energy. Key claim boundary: grid and power availability as a chokepoint is supported by recent industry reporting, but the degree to which each candidate converts AI/data-center demand into durable earnings remains an inference requiring backlog, customer, margin, and regulatory verification.
